title: Prevent an APM WAL from replacing another WAL lock sidecar
business_goal: Prevent WAL ownership bypass and split-brain recovery caused by a WAL path replacing another manager’s locked sidecar.
current_behavior: APM appends .lock to a resolved WAL path. A separate manager may use that sidecar as its WAL and atomically replace it, allowing another process to lock a replacement inode while the original owner still holds the old inode.
expected_behavior: Each supported effective WAL maps to one stable lock identity outside the replaceable WAL namespace. Alias or lock failures reject before recovery/admission; unsupported hard-link aliases fail closed.
in_scope: Offline path alias and process collision tests
acceptance_criteria: Pre-fix independent process reproduction demonstrates sidecar inode replacement and concurrent owners.
Post-fix collision fails before WAL mutation and third owner is denied while original owner is alive.
Relative, dot-segment, parent symlink and leaf symlink aliases share ownership; hard-linked WAL fails closed.
Lock identity remains stable across WAL atomic replacement and owner death; successor recovery is tested.
R3 regression set runs on exact new source with baseline failures separately classified.
Unknown deployment filesystem is reported DEPLOYMENT_UNVERIFIED.
safety_constraints: No broker, order, live process, deployment, commit, push, or merge action.
architecture_impact: Changes only APM WAL identity/ownership and its tests; no strategy or broker interface changes.
qa_attack_plan: Symlink, relative, dot-segment and hard-link alias tests
Lock path replacement and inode comparison
Crash during persistence and successor recovery
Unsupported flock and malformed lock path fail-closed cases
uat_criteria: R4 report explains collision and disposition with exact hashes and commands.
Report preserves DEPLOYMENT_UNVERIFIED and does not claim live readiness.
Unchanged smoke IN_FLIGHT assertion is explained without weakening OR trust.
release_gates: Do not claim merge or production readiness from selected tests.
rollback_plan: Stop all APM managers before rollback. Restore only the scoped APM code/test files; preserve WAL and lock artifacts. Never unlink lock files while an owner could remain.

state_history.reason: R4 requirements and acceptance criteria recorded.
Hermes contract defines stable ownership identity and explicit tests; PO and BA criteria are linked.
User authorized a local R4 hierarchy; BA/PO criteria and Hermes architecture are accepted; Grill Me collision and hard-link risks are explicitly in scope for fail-closed coverage.

evidence_standard.applicability_reason: The WAL ownership claim is material to durable recovery and entry admission.

claims.statement: For every supported APM WAL identity, one manager owns a stable lock identity that a WAL replacement or supported path alias cannot bypass.

assumptions.statement: Supported APM writers use ActivePositionManager and honor its ownership check.

claims.limitation: Post-fix QA and deployment filesystem evidence are not yet available.
